stories.headline: Procgen ingress gets a coordinate fix for maps without a TileSet
stories.summary: A new main-branch change repairs tile/world coordinate conversions during TileSet-free procedural candidate evaluation and adds a focused regression test. A seed-123456 sandbox startup is reported, but broader validation remains unresolved due to LFS import and authored-level registry failures.
stories.body: Procedural generation can evaluate candidate layouts before a visual TileSet is populated. The ingress spawner now delegates tile-to-world mapping to the procgen tilemap's shared conversion contract, while reverse conversion uses the native 32-pixel structural grid when no TileSet is present. A focused regression covers positive, origin and negative tiles in both TileSet-free and TileSet-backed modes. The commit reports a user-confirmed manual seed-123456 sandbox startup, not independently verified full CI. Existing broader LFS import and authored-level registry failures still need follow-up. This landing does not prove independent acceptance, deployment or teardown.

Focused regression added to validation manifest.

Next gate: run focused validation and resolve or isolate baseline-wide failures.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has landed a targeted procedural-generation fix for an awkward moment in level creation: evaluating a map before its visual tiles are ready. The change keeps world entrances aligned with the same 32-pixel grid used by structural generation.

sections.heading: Why a missing TileSet matters
sections.text: The world ingress spawner previously relied on a tilemap conversion that assumes a populated visual TileSet. Candidate evaluation can run earlier. It now uses the procgen map's shared conversion method, while reverse lookup handles that TileSet-free phase explicitly.

sections.heading: A regression is in place, but validation is not finished
sections.text: A new test checks coordinate round-trips with and without a TileSet, including negative tile coordinates. The commit reports a manual sandbox startup for seed 123456. Broader validation still has LFS import and authored-level registry failures, so this is a landed repair, not a clean project-wide acceptance.

insights.title: The structural grid is now the common reference
insights.explanation: Using the same coordinate contract in ingress and procgen reduces disagreement between candidate evaluation and later rendered maps.

insights.title: A focused test does not clear unrelated CI
insights.explanation: The new regression is useful evidence of intent and coverage, but the outstanding broader failures still require an independently inspected validation result.

article.takeaway: A targeted procgen coordinate repair is on main; independent validation and broader CI disposition remain open.
article.next_watch: Watch for a recorded focused regression PASS and a clear disposition of LFS import and authored-level registry failures.

stories.headline: Awakening gains its first production score, with transition-safe music handoff
stories.summary: The approved 'A Command Still Speaking' cue is now integrated into Awakening's production scene. New ownership logic keeps music through the ten-part sequence and releases it on successful Hub transition, while preserving playback after a failed handoff. The author reports 35/35 changed-file validations and an independent code recheck, but audible listening and canonical teardown remain unverified.

This is not a formal paired-review acceptance receipt, nor proof of audible loop quality. The cue's in-game seam and mixing still require human listening; host cleanup remains unknown.

article.lead: Awakening now has a production music cue. 'A Command Still Speaking' is wired into the opening sequence with rules that keep the score playing across scene beats and release it cleanly when the player reaches the Hub. The change reaches beyond adding an audio file: it handles failed transitions without abruptly losing the music.

sections.heading: Music that follows the scene, not the loading screen
sections.text: A dedicated director uses the existing two-deck music manager. It keeps the score through ten Awakening sections and optional Chapel content. On a successful Hub handoff, the cue fades without bringing back the prior playlist; a failed transition keeps the cue under Awakening's ownership.

sections.heading: Tests cover the real transition
sections.text: The first focused test did not exercise the production handoff path. After an independent code-review finding, the author added a regression that runs the actual transition and rollback behavior. The implementation summary reports 35 passing changed-file validations and a successful graphical startup, but no audible playback check.

insights.title: The transition boundary was the real risk
insights.explanation: The important fix is not just starting music, but preventing a successful transition from restoring an unwanted playlist and a failed transition from silencing the scene. The new regression targets that behavior.

insights.title: Green audio tests cannot certify the listening experience
insights.explanation: Technical validation supports scene integration and ownership behavior. It cannot establish whether the loop seam is audible or the mix feels right during gameplay; that remains a human audition.

article.takeaway: The Awakening score is integrated on main with meaningful regression coverage, while listening approval and verified host closeout remain separate gates.

stories.headline: Field Scout playtest route clarified; finding and restoring the buggy still need proof
stories.summary: New CUSTODIAN documentation explains why the Field Scout does not appear in the default Awakening launch and how to enter its Contract sandbox. It also exposes unresolved gameplay gaps: the wreck may not be placed within reach, uses placeholder hover art, and charges raw resources instead of the approved fabricated assemblies. These are documented limitations, not new runtime fixes.
stories.body: Main commits 389df928 and 50f20cd9 update the current-state guide and Godot app README. The default F5 project run starts Awakening, which has no Field Scout; the authored wreck is in the Contract sandbox, entered through the explicit --custodian-start=contract-sandbox argument. F6 runs a selected scene rather than the project entrypoint. The vehicle loader seeks eligible parking, road or compound tiles but may leave the authored position when no candidate passes filtering. No fixed-seed reachability receipt was inspected. The wreck begins disabled, still renders hover compatibility frames, and uses a raw-resource recovery profile instead of the approved three fabricated assemblies. Existing recovery correction/review, Asset V2 vehicle family and vehicle-placement extraction packets own these gaps. Both new commits are documentation-only; no gameplay fix, independent review, canonical teardown or live host execution was established.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now explains how to find its first Field Scout buggy, and why players may still miss it. The vehicle belongs to a development-only Contract sandbox, not the default Awakening opening. New guidance also makes clear that spawning the wreck, seeing the right artwork and restoring it as designed are three different unfinished hurdles.

sections.heading: The right door into the sandbox
sections.text: The normal project launch opens Awakening, which has no Scout. An explicit Contract sandbox startup argument loads the scene containing the vehicle. The docs now distinguish Godot's F5 project run from F6's current-scene run, preventing a misleading playtest.

sections.heading: A vehicle can exist without being discoverable
sections.text: The generated world attempts to relocate the authored wreck to eligible parking, road or compound space. If no tile qualifies, its original scene position can remain. Existing smoke tests do not establish that a player can find the Scout at a fixed seed.

sections.heading: The wreck is not yet its final form
sections.text: The Scout starts disabled and uses placeholder hover art instead of its approved wheeled body. Its current repair recipe consumes raw resources rather than the three fabricated assemblies required by the approved restoration design. Separate queued workstreams own these changes.

insights.title: Scene presence is not a playable encounter
insights.explanation: A node in the Godot scene tree proves neither that it lands on reachable terrain nor that players can discover it. The next useful proof is a fixed-seed runtime placement and reachability test.

insights.title: Restoration and presentation are separate gates
insights.explanation: A working vehicle class does not establish the approved visual identity or resource economy. The Asset V2 family and recovery correction need their own implementation and review evidence.

article.takeaway: The playtest route is documented more accurately, but this is not a new gameplay implementation or accepted Scout release.
article.next_watch: Watch for a fixed-seed placement/reachability receipt, the fabricated-assembly recovery correction and canonical wheeled-body asset integration.
